analog_aspect: Impact structure in basalt; impact breccia and glass
cafe_chapter: CAFE executive-summary site index (Lonar Crater); external USGS paper explicitly supports lunar crater comparison.
coord_source: Impact Earth centre coordinate (19°58′36″N, 76°30′30″E); bbox approximately covers the small crater and immediate rim.
note: Lonar is only about 1.8 km across and formed under Earth gravity/atmosphere; it is not a scale or environment match for a large lunar basin. Bounding box is a coarse crater envelope. Rationale: Peer-reviewed / USGS material describes Lonar as an impact crater formed in basalt and explicitly notes opportunities for comparison with lunar craters and Apollo impact products. This is a strong lithology-plus-impact-process comparator.
catalogue_status: Lonar Crater appears in the accessible CAFE executive-summary site index; exact catalogue target row/page not independently extracted.
target_pair_status: USGS describes a basalt-hosted impact crater compared with lunar craters; the target pairing is our mapping.
analogy_dimension: Impact structure in basalt; impact breccia and glass
review_action: Keep as a positive comparator for basalt-hosted impact features, but score lithology and impact morphology as separate dimensions.
